children: The contract covers 160 weapons under the Buy (Indian–Indigenously Designed, Developed and Manufactured) category

The Ministry of Defence (MoD) on Wednesday signed a contract worth Rs 810.79 crore with state-owned Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL) for the procurement of 160 Satellite Smart Anti-Airfield Weapons (SAT-SAAW) for the Indian Air Force (IAF).
The contract was signed under the Buy (Indian–Indigenously Designed, Developed and Manufactured) category in the presence of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh in New Delhi.

SAT-SAAW is an air-to-ground precision-guided glide bomb designed to target and disable enemy airfield infrastructure from a stand-off range. The weapon can be launched from fighter aircraft including the Jaguar, Hawk and Su-30 MKI.

The system has been designed and developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and has an indigenous content of around 60 per cent. The Ministry of Defence said key sub-systems, including the Initial Measurement Unit, Long Impact Delay Fuse and Twin Store Carrier, have also been indigenised.
According to the ministry, deliveries are scheduled between fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2029.
The weapon is intended to target infrastructure such as runways, taxiways, aircraft hangars, reinforced bunkers and radar installations while allowing aircraft to operate from a safe distance.

The SAT variant combines satellite navigation through GPS and NavIC with an onboard Inertial Navigation System (INS) to strike stationary targets with high accuracy in all weather conditions, during both day and night operations.
